title: HTML smuggling
overview: Compare attachment-inspection results for normal HTML and a sandbox-classified generated artifact.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and mail gateway or attachment projection fields.

attack.name: HTML Smuggling
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: An HTML attachment that materializes an embedded file in sandbox telemetry warrants message triage.
evidence: Identify attachment type, sandbox trait and message ID. Correlate delivery and endpoint follow-on evidence.
false_positive: An internal export can embed a harmless downloadable report.
tuning: Distinguish allowed publishers and sandbox artifact traits. Test exceptions against archived positive examples.
response: Quarantine matching messages, preserve sandbox metadata and review user interaction and downloaded-file events.
prevention: Apply HTML attachment controls, approved sandboxes and browser download policy.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The event is a sandbox verdict. No HTML attachment or active content is included.

questions.prompt: Which field separates the two HTML records?
questions.explanation: Both examples are HTML. Materialization is the differentiating observation.

questions.prompt: How do you check user impact?
options: Assume a gateway verdict proves execution
Correlate delivery with endpoint and click evidence
questions.explanation: Message scanning and endpoint execution refer to different stages.
